overview: Two of the most important differential stains in microbiology, distinguishing organisms based on very different cell wall chemistry.
genZNote: Gram stain reads the wall. Acid-fast reads the wax coat over it.

aspects.label: Principle
aspects.valueA: Exploits mycolic acid in the cell wall, which resists decolorization by acid-alcohol once carbolfuchsin is heat-fixed in.
aspects.valueB: Exploits differences in peptidoglycan thickness, determining whether crystal violet-iodine complex is retained or washed out.

aspects.label: Target Organisms
aspects.valueA: Mycobacterium species (e.g. M. tuberculosis) and some Nocardia species with mycolic acid-rich walls.
aspects.valueB: Virtually all bacteria, classified as Gram-positive or Gram-negative.

aspects.label: Result Interpretation
aspects.valueA: Acid-fast organisms retain pink/red carbolfuchsin; non-acid-fast organisms stain blue with methylene blue.
aspects.valueB: Gram-positive organisms stain purple; Gram-negative organisms stain pink/red.

aspects.label: Clinical Relevance
aspects.valueA: Key diagnostic step for suspected tuberculosis and other mycobacterial or nocardial infections.
aspects.valueB: First-line categorization for essentially any unidentified bacterial isolate.

aspects.label: Limitations / Pitfalls
aspects.valueA: Does not distinguish between different acid-fast species; requires additional culture/molecular testing for identification.
aspects.valueB: Old/dying cells can over-decolorize and appear falsely Gram-negative.

aspects.label: Key Distinguishing Feature
aspects.valueB: Detects peptidoglycan thickness (all bacteria); crystal violet/iodine/safranin.
